about: St Brannock's, the village chapel, a room file v2 (the format: the builder's README, room files). Metres in the room's frame: x east, y north, z up, the floor's centre on the origin; 16 x 10 m inside (x -8..8, y -5..5), 4.5 m high. Every prop, spot, portal and night light of packages/content/data/scenes/chapel.json is named below. The chapel faces north: the altar under the north lancets with a candle stand either side, the lectern and the pulpit at the chancel step, three rows of box pews down the nave either side of the aisle (x 0.5), the font, the alms box and the votive rack by the east door; five lancets of stained glass (G14's lancet), two of them moon-lit; the crypt stairs down in the south-west corner (G12's flight, D6). Grey boxes stand in for the pieces with no model (decision D2).
district_note: equal to the scene's `name`: cc_struct.py compares each spawn's wdi_district with it

spawn_labels.crypt: At the head of the crypt stairs

height_note: the plan's 4.5 m for the chapel (Reference E)
floor_note: the nave's flags (`f` in the scene's material layer) over the whole floor, as the manor hall's: the chancel's boards (`w`) and the crypt corner's earth (`d`) wait for G11's floor by tile letter
wall_colour_note: guess: old limewash over stone, a warm grey; yellow-brown above blue, never pink or lilac under the moon and the candles
wood_colour_note: dark oak: the door, the pews, the beams, the crypt stairs
skirting_note: none: limewashed stone to the flags
picture_rail_note: none, and the lancets rise to 4.1 m
cornice_note: none: the walls meet the roof boards

openings.note: the chapel door in the east wall, tile (17,6): centred at y -0.5, the portal at its foot (8.0, -0.5); the door spawn stands 0.5 m inside it, (7.5, -0.5), facing west up the nave's cross aisle. 1.1 m wide (the barn's: cc_geom's door check measures 0.6 m either side of the centre) and 2.4 m high: a panel door until G13's double door

openings.flight_note: G12 (D6: visible stairs): a crypt stair against the west wall, 0.9 m wide (x -8.0..-7.1, y -5.0..-3.0, tiles (1,9) and (1,10)), its head at the south wall, descending north and on 1 m under the flags into the dark; a balustrade on its north and east edges. Its two tiles cannot be stood on (listed for the owner): a 0.6 m well with no east rail kept them, but the open edge was an invisible wall (cc_geom, the first no-bake build), and with a rail any well leaves too little of the tiles. The portal at the scene's tile (2,11), its foot on the south wall's face (-6.5, -5.0), 0.9 m east of the stair's head; the crypt spawn (-6.5, -4.5) stands beside the head, facing north
openings.note: the crypt stairs down to the cellar (ch.crypt: to cellar, spawn crypt, 3 m down)

the five lancets (G14's lancet): 0.7 m wide, the sill at 2.0 m and the apex at 4.1 m (the arch springs at 3.49 m), in a dressed stone surround on the wall face, a lead grid of 3 x 9 quarries: a blue border and foot, amber, red and green in turn up the middle, gold in the head. Over 1.75 m: nothing of them is an invisible wall. This one at tile (3,0), x -5.5, dark (no moon light names it)
at tile (11,0), x 2.5: the moon comes through it (ch.lt_moon_window)
the west wall's first lancet, tile (0,4), y 1.5, dark
the west wall's second, tile (0,8), y -2.5: the moon comes through it (ch.lt_moon_nave)

openings_note: the five lancets say no `outside`: the room has no `outside` block, so each is `sky` (a backdrop on the north wall and one on the west, decision 10 of the builder's design)

moon.note: one Sun for the room (R-L9): the moon-lit lancets stand on the north and the west walls, so a compass bearing toward the moon, north-west, a little higher than the bedroom's 32 degrees

exposure_note: null: chosen from the bake (the builder's choose_exposure)

lights.note: the altar's west candle (tile (8,1)): the candlestick's flame on its tall stand, stronger than a room's lamp (the altar's light carries the chapel)

the votive candles on their rack (tile (15,3)): one light at the rack's top, seven small flames in two rows, their feet on the rack's top (2.3 cm under the light: the first no-bake build found them floating)
the moon through the north wall's third lancet (tile (11,0))
the moon through the west wall's second lancet (tile (0,8)). The scene's day light ch.lt_window_east is a day and dusk light: the walk is night only

lights_note: Bake groups: candle (the altar's two candles and the votives), moon (the two lancets) and fill = 3, and the AO.

chapel.label: the chapel
chapel.note: the first guess (moon 3.0, fill 0.3, from the parlour and the barn) gave a first 128-sample bake (2026-11-22) whose moon patch read 0.003 to 0.014 on the display (lost) and 93 % of the vertices under the ink before the lift: the moon through the narrow lancets and the fill raised for the second bake (moon 8, fill 0.6: the patch 0.012 to 0.061). From the second bake's saved light, moon 16 and fill 1.2 gave 0.039 to 0.127, the shafts on the west wall and the floor seen; the exposure follows the candles' pool (E 0.39 to 0.40 in all three), so the nave stays a dark church at night
